mentions.name: Bitwit
mentions.description: Bitwit is a spaced-repetition education site for computer science and math. It presents study cards, with TeX/MathJax support for math formatting, and can be used for an extended period (several months to a few years) without requiring an email address or signup.

mentions.name: Bitwit
mentions.description: A web app for learning CS, logic, and math theory (not DSA) via spaced repetition combined with parametrically generated problems. Successive presentations of the same card generate a different problem instance and validate solutions randomly and parametrically, so learners absorb the invariants each card teaches instead of memorizing variable-value combinations — described as a kind of MathAcademy for CS. Subjects include Boolean Logic and Lambda Calculus (free forever) plus other subjects whose first topic is free.
mentions.problem: The author had poor results learning CS/math with Anki and other flash card systems; without problems exercising the tools and techniques, they would evaporate from memory, motivating the combination of spaced repetition with generated problem practice.
mentions.audience: Learners studying CS, logic, and math theory; the author invites anyone curious to try it for free (Boolean Logic and Lambda Calculus subjects free forever, first topic of other subjects free).
